rules.commentary: Pressure residual is oscillating rather than decreasing monotonically — the last few iterations show alternating amplitude > 30% of the mean. This commonly indicates the pressure-relaxation factor is too aggressive for the case's coupling strength. Consider lowering `relaxationFactors.p` in system/fvSolution (e.g., 0.3 → 0.2) and re-running. If oscillation persists, check the under-relaxation on the momentum equation as well. Reference: Ferziger & Perić, Computational Methods for Fluid Dynamics — under-relaxation and iterative-convergence stability.
rules.provenance: Ferziger & Perić · Computational Methods for Fluid Dynamics · under-relaxation & iterative-convergence stability

rules.commentary: Solver reached its iteration cap (maxIters from system/fvSolution → solvers section) WITHOUT meeting the convergence tolerance. The case is technically not finished — the residuals at the final iter represent the best the solver achieved in the budget. Three common causes: (1) under-relaxation too aggressive (lower the values), (2) mesh quality issue creating an ill-conditioned linear system (run checkMesh and look at maxNonOrtho / maxSkewness), (3) BC/IC inconsistency producing an unsolvable steady state. Inspect the residual trajectory: if it was still decreasing at termination, simply increase maxIters. If it had plateaued, root-cause one of the three above. Reference: Versteeg & Malalasekera, An Introduction to CFD — iterative convergence and termination criteria.
rules.provenance: Versteeg & Malalasekera · An Introduction to CFD · iterative convergence & termination criteria

rules.commentary: The solver process exited with a non-zero status code, which means it died before reporting convergence. This is distinct from "hit maxIters but kept running cleanly" (see R2). Likely causes: floating-point exception (NaN in a field — often from an unstable initial timestep), missing dictionary entry that wasn't caught by case validation, or an unsupported solver feature for the case configuration. Check the log file (BottomPanel → Log tab) for the FOAM error message; that text typically pins the root cause within a few lines. Reference: Ferziger & Perić §8.7 on stability and Versteeg & Malalasekera §7.5 on debugging.
rules.provenance: Ferziger & Perić · Computational Methods for Fluid Dynamics · §8.7

rules.commentary: Maximum absolute deviation from the gold-standard reference exceeds 5%. For canonical cases (Ghia 1982 lid-driven cavity, etc.), agreement within 1-3% is the expected bar. Drift of this magnitude usually points to: (1) mesh too coarse near the wall (yPlus too high — try refining boundary layers), (2) wrong turbulence model selection for the Reynolds regime, (3) compressibility/incompressibility mismatch (check whether the case is actually low-Mach). Cross-check the case profile in `.planning/case_profiles/` for the canonical solver/mesh choices that match the gold reference. Reference: Roache, Verification and Validation in Computational Science and Engineering — validation against reference data.
rules.provenance: Roache · Verification and Validation in Computational Science and Engineering · solution validation against reference data

rules.commentary: Drag/lift coefficients are still changing >1% between the last 10 iterations — the integral quantities haven't settled even though residuals may have. This often happens in steady-state cases that are actually transient (vortex shedding off bluff bodies, separated flow regions). Three things to check: (1) is this a Re/geometry regime that should be running pimpleFoam (transient) rather than simpleFoam (steady)? (2) are the force-monitoring patches the right ones? (3) is the case at a long-enough integration time? Reference: Ferziger & Perić §13.6 on unsteady RANS vs steady RANS regimes.
rules.provenance: Ferziger & Perić · Computational Methods for Fluid Dynamics · §13.6

rules.commentary: Run took 5000+ iterations to converge — the case worked, but at the long end of typical effort. This is often a hint that (a) the initial guess (potentialFoam pre-step, or zero initialization) was far from the final state, or (b) the under-relaxation is conservative enough that you're trading robustness for speed. If you're iterating on this case, consider warmer starts (use the previous run's final fields as IC) or slightly more aggressive relaxation factors. Reference: Versteeg & Malalasekera, An Introduction to CFD — convergence acceleration.
rules.provenance: Versteeg & Malalasekera · An Introduction to CFD · convergence acceleration

rules.commentary: Velocity residual has plateaued (last 20 iterations show variation <2% but value is still 10× above the convergence tolerance). The solver isn't going to improve from here without intervention. Likely causes: (1) under-relaxation too conservative for this regime — try increasing relaxationFactors.U from 0.7 → 0.85, (2) the linear-solver tolerance (in fvSolution → solvers → U) is set too loose so each outer iteration leaves residual behind, (3) the boundary conditions are over-constraining the system (e.g., velocity prescribed on too many patches without a free outlet). Reference: Ferziger & Perić, Computational Methods for Fluid Dynamics — residual stalling and iterative convergence.
rules.provenance: Ferziger & Perić · Computational Methods for Fluid Dynamics · residual stalling & iterative convergence

rules.commentary: Pressure residual decreased monotonically over the last 8 iterations and the run converged within budget — this is the textbook "things going right" pattern. No action needed. If you're tuning this case for a parameter sweep, this is a good baseline to reuse the relaxation/scheme choices from. Reference: Versteeg & Malalasekera §11.3 on convergence acceleration.
rules.provenance: Versteeg & Malalasekera · An Introduction to CFD · §11.3

rules.commentary: The pressure residual has climbed monotonically over the last several iterations and crossed O(1) — the solution is diverging, not converging. Because OpenFOAM residuals are normalized to roughly 1.0 at startup, a residual that grows past its starting value means the outer iteration is unstable. Common roots: a Courant number / timestep that is too aggressive, zero turbulence initial conditions (k-ωSST divides by √k, so near-zero wall k sends ω toward infinity — V3), an unbounded mass-flow or velocity inlet on a zero initial field (V6), or a thermophysical bound violation such as negative density in compressible flow (V7). Reduce relaxation/timestep, warm-start from potentialFoam or a laminar pass, and confirm the IC/BC are physical before re-running. Reference: Ferziger & Perić §8.7 on iterative stability.
rules.provenance: docs/openfoam_corpus/industrial_solver_findings_v_series.md · V3 (kOmegaSST ω blowup) · V6 (mass-flow zero-IC divergence) · V7 (compressible ρ negative) · Ferziger & Perić §8.7

rules.commentary: Scalar gold-delta breaches the 5% R4 floor, BUT the developed region (x ≥ developed_region_min_m = 0.1 m, an order of magnitude past NASA TMR's LE exclusion x<0.01) carries ZERO per-point failures AND the NASA-convention dual-metric gate (integrated-Cf drag + Cf@verification_station) is within tolerance. The remaining high pointwise rel_error lives in the near-LE band cataloged as `known_deviations` — the OpenFOAM-kΩSST-vs-CFL3D formulation discrepancy that survived correct Re + NASA topology + freestream + y+~1 + 4× grid refinement (DEC-V61-209 cycle-3g). This is a HONEST KNOWN KNOWN, not a fresh anomaly: scalar max_abs_pct is poisoned by near-LE noise the canonical NASA comparison was never meant to score. Treat as the demoted near-LE deviation pattern; do not re-litigate the scalar drift. Cross-check DEC-V61-209 ADDENDUM 5 #2 and the `reference_comparison.csv known_deviations` block. Reference: DEC-V61-209 ADDENDUM 5 + Roache, V&V — regional vs scalar validation.
rules.provenance: .planning/decisions/2026-05-27_v61_209_flat_plate_vv_de_fake.md · ADDENDUM 5 #2 (lines 380-404, near-LE known_deviations scope) · ADDENDUM 3 cycle-3g (lines 266-275, OpenFOAM-kΩSST-vs-CFL3D formulation discrepancy) · Roache · V&V §regional vs scalar metrics

rules.commentary: The developed region (x ≥ developed_region_min_m = 0.1 m, past NASA TMR's LE exclusion x<0.01) carries one or more per-point failures with max rel_error > 5%. This is qualitatively DIFFERENT from scalar amplitude drift (R4): a per-point shape mismatch past the LE-exclusion floor points to a solver-side bug — wrong turbulence model variant, BC inconsistency producing a localized spike, or post-processing stride bug — NOT discretization or known near-LE formulation discrepancy. DEC-V61-209 ADDENDUM 5 #1 added the developed-region guard because integral-drag + a single verification station cannot reject a curve whose +/- area errors cancel in the integral AND happens to match at the one station. An out-of-tolerance point at x ≥ 0.1 m is a real FAIL, not a `known_deviation` laundering candidate. Cross-check DEC-V61-209 ADDENDUM 5 and `trust_report.json reference_comparison.developed_region.failures`. Reference: Versteeg & Malalasekera §10 on regional vs scalar V&V.

rules.commentary: The two NASA-canonical metrics DISAGREE on PASS/FAIL: integrated-Cf drag rel_error and Cf@x=0.97008 station rel_error are scored against the same 10% tolerance, but one crosses the boundary while the other does not. Because the same run is graded by two NASA-corroborating methods, divergence itself is a citable finding — typically a post-processing / integration-pipeline bug, not a CFD issue. DEC-V61-209 lines 226-231 document the canonical incident: `cfdtrust run` did NOT clean stale time directories before solving, so the integration arithmetic ran on the wrong field while the station readout happened to be right. Advisory: trust the integrated number, distrust the station post-processing (or vice versa); inspect the case dir for stale time directories, mismatched wall face counts, or a verification_station off the extracted-field grid. Cross-check DEC-V61-209 ADDENDUM 4 + lines 226-231. Reference: Ferziger & Perić §13.6 on integrated vs pointwise V&V.
rules.provenance: .planning/decisions/2026-05-27_v61_209_flat_plate_vv_de_fake.md · ADDENDUM 4 (lines 304-339, NASA-convention dual-metric gate) + lines 226-231 (stale time-dir integration-pipeline bug incident) · Ferziger & Perić §13.6 integrated vs pointwise V&V

rules.commentary: Dangling coupled-interface reference detected at the region-inventory level: a coupled boundary patch on a region declares a neighbour_region that is absent from the assembled multi-region inventory. This is the slice-level shadow of the V94 death-chain — a coupled-patch BC referencing a counterpart that does not resolve in the per-region polyMesh produces solver FATAL 'Cannot find patchField entry for region_hot_fluid_to_domain0'. The check is a region-inventory integrity test (not a patch-level existence test): if cp.neighbour_region is declared but that region name does not appear in the slice's region inventory, the interface reference is dangling. Advisory: verify every coupled interface's neighbour_region is declared in regionProperties and has a resolved non-zero-cell cellZone in the final polyMesh. This predicate WOULD fire on the actual V94 input shape (unlike the prior case-wide coupling-type family heuristic).

rules.commentary: A region is listed in the CHT region inventory but carries NO per-region thermophysical model payload (both thermo_type and thermo_snapshot_ref are absent/None). V14 death-chain: chtMultiRegionSimpleFoam crashed mid-Time=1 (radiation setup), no time directory beyond 0/ was written, and the post-processor reading solid-region T fields hit the OpenFOAM missing-field sentinel ±1e+300 — a per-region payload that was never produced, masquerading as catastrophic divergence. V92 structural twin: region_solid silently got 0 cells and was absent from the final polyMesh, so a region listed in regionProperties had no resolvable thermo/field payload (mesh_summary FAIL: only 2/3 expected regions present; missing region_solid). Advisory: check constant/<region>/thermophysicalProperties for every declared region and confirm the extractor ran over each region.

rules.commentary: Zero-fluid region inventory detected: every classified region in the CHT slice is solid, so no convective momentum source can drive inter-region heat exchange. Fires on V92-class fluid-region loss (fluid region silently got 0 cells, dropped from polyMesh, inventory becomes all-solid) or a genuinely conduction-only case. KNOWN GAP: the BC-driven v5b degeneracy (fluid regions PRESENT but kinematically dead — all-walls fixedValue (0,0,0), no mass flow → pure-conduction collapse at iter 200) is NOT detectable from the current slice schema. RegionSlice carries no kinematic-BC or mass-flow field; R15 detects only the zero-fluid-topology case. Advisory: if this fires unexpectedly, verify each fluid region has a non-zero-cell cellZone in the final polyMesh and non-trivial inlet/outlet BCs.

Four V-row death-chains: V94 (STL no face-zone labels → sHM one undifferentiated patch per region pair → named patches absent); V85 (insidePoint inside hot-fluid layer + 0.8mm plates → cellZone leak → region_hot_fluid absent from polyMesh); V90 (modern locationsInMesh syntax on separate-STL multi-region → empty named cellZones, only 1 of 3 populated); V92 (cellZoneInside on fuse_many void STL → region_solid 0 cells, missing from polyMesh). Advisory: run a pre-solve snappyHexMesh face-zone audit — confirm every declared region resolves to a non-zero-cell cellZone in the final polyMesh before handing off to chtMultiRegionSimpleFoam.
